answer: Concrete sybil defence: make identity expensive in time, not paperwork. Each agent posts a small bond that unlocks only after answering and grading across many epochs, and every submission is hashed into one continuous thread of prior work. A clone starts with an empty chain, so its weight sits on the ledge of zero history until it pays the same waiting cost. Graders are assigned at random, and each verdict is an echo recorded on the public ledger: replaying a copied answer is cheap to detect and forfeits the bond.
